title: Drop the dead v1 expected-decision mapping from the declaration compiler
summary: compile_plugin_contract built a final_results dictionary that translated each plugin business-case conclusion (ready, rework, needs_review, not_applicable) into the retired v1 result vocabulary (scanned_no_issue, issue_found, needs_review, not_applicable) and stored the translation as expectedDecision on an internal business_cases record. Nothing read that field: the compiled Plugin Contract only ever emitted expected.final with the business word, business_cases is not returned, and no document or test named expectedDecision. This change deletes the dead translation, validates the case conclusion against the business vocabulary directly, and adds an architecture-gate guard so expectedDecision cannot return. No compiled contract field, plugin case schema, runtime behaviour, or published artifact changes: the compiled output is byte-for-byte the same. Verification evidence: the change landed in fc37484, pushed on 2026-09-17 with fc37484 as the publish point, and CI run 35215830428 passed all seven jobs (Fast on Python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13, Full on 3.11 and 3.13, and Install matrix on 3.11 and 3.13 including the clean-environment compiled acceptance); locally the architecture check returns 0 with eighteen boundary tests passing, the compiled plugin.json for the policy-pack fixture is byte-for-byte identical before and after the change, the fast profile reported 431 tests OK and full reported 444 tests OK, the design confirmation gate passes over the cee6634..fc37484 range, and the document, plugin-source, English text and resilience gates all returned 0.

platform: Platform governance owns the declaration compiler and the architecture gate that guards retired v1 result vocabulary
plugin: No plugin change; plugin cases keep declaring ready, rework, needs_review, or not_applicable

forbiddenResponsibilities: The change must not alter the compiled Plugin Contract output, its schema, or any plugin case validation outcome
The change must not change any live decision state, Kernel gate, or the frozen v1 SDK schema
The change must not remove the business vocabulary from the compiled contract's expected.final field
acceptance: declaration_compiler.py contains no v1 result mapping and no expectedDecision field
the compiled Plugin Contract output is unchanged for the existing fixture plugins
the architecture gate rejects a reintroduced expectedDecision name
the architecture, document, plugin-source, English text and resilience gates return 0 and the fast and full profiles stay green

humanApproval.decision: Internal-only dead-code removal carried out under the standing authorization of the refactor mandate in #assayer-group:4c84ee19 and its delegation update, under which the agent and reviewer decide these changes themselves within at most seven workflow rounds. No compiled contract, schema, published artifact, contract, or live behaviour changes: the removed expectedDecision field was never read, and the compiled output is unchanged.
